rows.text: Form WR11: Water Resources Act 1991 (Section 199(1))
Notice of the intention to drill for minerals
Fill in this form to give us notice that you intend to drill for minerals.
Operator’s or organisation’s name

Address of the site where the drilling will be carried out (Unless we have agreed otherwise with you, you should provide an Ordnance Survey map showing the site or area of the drilling. Outline the site or area in red. The map must be at a scale of not less than 1:10,000.)
Postcode
Date of the drilling (Except in emergency, this date must be at least one month after the date of this notice.)
(DD/MM/YYYY)
What work will be carried out? (Please tick one box.)
Number of boreholes (You must provide a plan, at a scale of 1:2,500, showing the position of each borehole.)
On a separate sheet, numbered 1, provide the national grid reference (two letters, 10 numbers) for each borehole.
Purpose of the work (Please tick one box.)
Give relevant details of the proposed work (for example, depth, diameter, orientation, method of construction or extension, strata and casing details).
If there is not enough space for your answer, provide the necessary information on a separate sheet numbered 2.
Explain how you will prevent fluid (including groundwater, brine, gases, natural and artificial contaminants such as hydrocarbons) flowing between different aquifer layers or the surface.
If there is not enough space for your answer, provide the necessary information on a separate sheet numbered 3.
Explain how you will use and dispose of water and fluids entering the borehole or boreholes
If there is not enough space for your answer, provide the necessary information on a separate sheet numbered 4.
Who should we contact about this notice?
Contact’s name and address
Name
Address
Postcode
By signing below, you are confirming that you are authorised to give this notice and that, as far as you know and believe, the information you have provided is accurate.
Your signature
Date (DD/MM/YYYY)
Send this notice, along with any supporting information, to your local Environment Agency office.
WR11 Version 2, March 2019

This wholly fictional benchmark example is neither regulatory advice nor a submission-ready notice. The operator is Example Mineral Research Ltd. The two site-address lines, in source order, are Demonstration Test Plot and Example Research Grounds. Site postcode: ZZ1 1ZZ. This postcode is an intentionally non-real placeholder. The notice is dated 18/09/2026 and the planned drilling date is 20/10/2026, more than one month later. The number of boreholes is 1. The planned work is Constructing a borehole or boreholes, not extending an existing borehole. The purpose is Searching for minerals, not extracting minerals.

Give relevant details of the proposed work (for example, depth, diameter, orientation, method of construction or extension, strata and casing details). One vertical exploratory borehole, nominal depth 12 m and diameter 100 mm; the fictional design and casing schedule are subject to specialist approval.

Explain how you will prevent fluid (including groundwater, brine, gases, natural and artificial contaminants such as hydrocarbons) flowing between different aquifer layers or the surface. A qualified contractor will apply the approved isolation and sealing design; work will stop if unexpected groundwater conditions occur.

Explain how you will use and dispose of water and fluids entering the borehole or boreholes Collect all returning water and fluids in closed containers for characterisation and transfer through an authorised waste contractor; no surface discharge is planned.

For contact about the notice, select Operator only; neither Agent nor Professional adviser is the nominated contact. The operator's fictional contact name is Alex Morgan; contact address: 1 Fictional Research Way, Exampletown; contact postcode: ZZ1 2ZZ, another intentionally non-real placeholder. Alex is authorised in this fictional scenario. Enter the typed placeholder Alex Morgan (synthetic signature) in Your signature and 18/09/2026 in Date (DD/MM/YYYY). No real signature, personal data, location, map or national-grid coordinate is supplied. The source's map, plan and separate-sheet requirements remain visible, but supporting attachments are not generated or represented as completed submissions. The short narrative answers fit their respective fields without overflow sheets 2, 3 or 4.
